description.cancellation_policy:
Cancellation Policy: Reservations cancelled 3 or more full days before the reservation start date receive a full refund of the recreation (per-person, per-night) fee. Reservations cancelled less than 3 days before the reservation start date are non-refundable. The $10 reservation fee is non-refundable.  

Change Policy: you may make changes to your permit itinerary (campsite locations), if space is available, up to two days before your reservation date. You may make changes to your group size and group member names up to the time your permit is issued. Additional fees may apply.  

Your start date cannot be changed without cancelling your existing reservation and booking a new reservation. 

One additional permit holder can be identified when the reservation is created. Otherwise, reservations and permits are non-transferrable.
description.comment_box_description: Please provide us with information such as if you are a Continental Divide hiker, or if you will be using an unlisted trailhead. If traveling by non motorized boat, please provide information as to the type of boat and/or if you are being dropped off by the Bridge Bay boat shuttle. For winter trips, please provide UTM’s or descriptions of where you will be camping each night, and the emergency equipment you will have (satellite messenger, shovel, beacon, probe, extra fuel, extra food, etc.)
description.description:
Hosting over 4 million visits annually, Yellowstone is the world’s first National Park preserving more than 10,000 hydrothermal features and countless wildlife including bison, grizzly bears, gray wolves, elk, and moose. The park forms the core of the Greater Yellowstone Ecosystem, one of the world’s largest, nearly intact temperate-zone ecosystems. 

Beyond the roads, boardwalks, and developed areas, Yellowstone National Park offers a diverse, mountainous landscape that invites exploration by foot, pack stock, and boat. With over 1,000 miles of trail, 293 designated campsites, and 3 lakes accessible for boating there are ample opportunities for adventure and solitude.
description.driving_directions:
Backcountry Permit Offices are located at Bridge Bay, Grant Village, South Entrance, West Yellowstone, Mammoth, Tower, and Bechler areas. Make sure to check the Backcountry Conditions Report for up-to-date office hours, and open locations.  When arriving in the park, check the NPS (National Park Service) App or the Park's newspaper for directions / maps to the Backcountry Permit Office locations or visit the Operating Dates to find a list of all office locations including Backcountry Offices. 

Groups traveling by boat may only pick up their permits at Bridge Bay, Grant Village, and South Entrance Backcountry Offices.
description.fee_policy:
• Early Access Lottery Application/Reservation Fee: $10 (non-refundable). The application fee is charged for all applications to the early access lottery (regardless of success) and for all other permit reservations.
  • Recreation Fee: $5 per person, per night plus the $10 non-refundable reservation fee (if the reservation is booked through the lottery, the $10 non-refundable reservation fee will not apply since you have already paid the $10 non-refundable lottery application fee). The recreation fee is charged year-round for permits secured through this website or in-person at a backcountry office.
  • Entrance Fee: Yellowstone charges an entrance fee separate from permit fees. You may pay the fee upon arrival or purchase in advance. The park honors valid America the Beautiful-the National Parks and Federal Recreational Lands passes (also known as an interagency passes, e.g., Senior, 4th Grade, Military, etc.). Visit the park's Fees & Passes web page.
description.lottery_information:
The early access lottery application period is March 1 - 20. To apply, you will submit your basic contact information, not a trip itinerary. We will notify you of the lottery results around March 25. Only one application per-person will be accepted. Applications from individuals submitting applications from multiple accounts will be canceled.

Successful applicants gain early access to reservations to build their trip itinerary and receive a date and time that their individual access window opens. Applicants may create a reservation at any time after their access window opens. Individuals are limited to a single reservation during the early access period but may create additional reservations beginning April 26. Large groups needing multiple campsites each night will need to submit separate applications with unique trip leaders.
description.need_to_know_email:
This is not your permit. You must check-in at a backcountry permit office in-person within 2 days of your trip start date to obtain your actual permit.  

  • Permits must be obtained in person during permit office hours of operation (8:00 AM-4:30 PM). Permits must be picked up by 10:00 AM on the first day of your permit or they may be canceled. 

  • If you are unable to pick up the permit by 10:00 AM, contact the Central Backcountry Office (307-344-2160) to have your permit held. 

  • If you are travelling by boat, you must obtain your permit at the following Backcountry Offices: Bridge Bay, Grant Village, or the South Entrance. All other permits can be obtained at any Backcountry Office. Please check the Backcountry Office Schedule closer to your arrival date for updated office hours and open locations. 

  • If you are unable to use your reservation, please cancel your trip as soon as possible, in consideration of other campers. Reservations cancelled 3 or more full days before the reservation start date receive a full refund of the user recreation fee. Reservations cancelled less than 3 days before the reservation start date are non-refundable. The $10 reservation fee is non-refundable.  

  • You may make changes to your permit itinerary up to two days before your reservation date. You may make changes to your group size and group member names up to the time your permit is issued. Additional fees may apply. Your start date cannot be changed without cancelling your existing reservation and booking a new reservation. 

  • You are responsible for knowing all park rules and regulations and conveying that information to all group members.

  • Make sure to review current backcountry trail conditions for your area of travel prior to your trip.  

  • During the non-peak/winter season (Nov 1-May 14), contact the Central Backcountry Office up to 5 days before your trip to obtain your permit.

  • Review the Stock Regulations if travelling with stock.

  • Review the Boating Regulations if travelling by boat.
description.need_to_know_order:
• You are making a reservation for backcountry campsites. This is not your permit. 

  • You must visit a backcountry office in person to obtain your permit and attend a park regulations and safety briefing. 

  • Your reservation is valid only for the dates, campsites, travel method, and number of people/stock listed.

  • Review the Fees & Cancellations page before continuing.

  • Campfires are not permitted at all campsites. Review campsite details to see if campfires are permitted at your campsites. 

  • Campsites and trails are subject to closures due to bear activity, wildfire, etc. If your campsite(s) or route are affected, we will make every effort to contact you and help you change your itinerary.

  • Proper food storage is required. Food poles or metal bear boxes are provided at designated backcountry campsites. Hard sided bear resistant food containers approved by the Interagency Grizzly Bear Committee are permitted and may be stored on the ground underneath the food pole, or 300 feet from sleeping areas where no food pole exists. 

  • Carrying bear spray is recommended.

  • The boating season is open May 24 - October 31. All watercraft, including float tubes, must purchase a Yellowstone boat permit and be inspected for Aquatic Invasive Species before launching. Inspections and boat permits are available 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM daily at Bridge Bay, Grant Village, and Lewis Lake. Additional fee required. Plan accordingly. 

  • Stock users must possess proof of a negative Coggins test performed within the last 12 months for all equine stock entering Yellowstone. 

  • Campers are limited to 3 consecutive nights in the Slough Creek drainage (sites 2S1-2S6) June 15-September 15. Reservations with more than 3 nights in Slough Creek will be modified.

  • Individuals may not be listed on multiple permits with overlapping dates.

  • You are responsible for knowing all park rules & regulations and conveying the information to all group members. 

  • Itineraries are subject to review and modification by backcountry staff.
description.need_to_know_permit:
This website provides access to view availability and to secure reservations for permits. Pre-plan your trip using the park's Camping in the Backcountry web page and other resources and guidebooks.

  • We encourage you to participate in the early access reservation lottery if you plan to camp in high-demand areas (e.g. Slough Creek, Bechler area, Heart Lake, and Shoshone Lake) during peak season.

  • You may not reserve non-standard itineraries (including long mileage, undesignated campsites, switching travel methods, or more than 14 nights) through Recreation.gov. Contact the Central Backcountry Office for help reserving a permit in these situations. 

  • During the early access lottery period, Central Backcountry Office staff are available to help Monday through Friday 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM. From May through early October, staff is available daily.

When planning your trip, please keep the following in mind:

  • Your reservation is not a permit. You must pick up permits in-person at a park Backcountry Permit Office within two days of the trip start date. 

  • Not all campsites are reservable in advance. Sites designated as "In-Station" and are only available in-person within two days of the trip start date.

  • You may need more than one permit if your trip is non-contiguous. A separate backcountry permit is required anytime you return to your vehicle and travel to a new trailhead.

  • You may stay up to 3 consecutive nights at any one campsite unless otherwise noted in the campsite description. Some campsites have 1- and 2-night limits. 

  • Obtaining multiple permits to bypass site restrictions (i.e night limit, travel method, etc.) is not permitted. 

  • Obtaining multiple permits with overlapping dates for the same individuals using different accounts is not permitted. 

  • Each campsite has a limit on the number of people, stock, and boats. If your group exceeds the number of people permitted at a campsite, you will need to split into separate groups and obtain separate permits with different trip leaders. Groups must cook, eat, and sleep separately. Affiliated groups may not congregate in a campsite if the total amount of people exceeds the campsite capacity. 

  • Camping in designated sites is required (except during the winter and in certain circumstances where designated sites do not exist, with approval from park staff).

  • Pay attention to the allowable travel method(s) for each campsite as listed in the campsite name: e.g., Backpacker, Stock, Llama, Non-Motorized Boat, Boat

    • You may not stay at a campsite that does not correspond to your method of travel.

    • Backpackers are not allowed to reserve campsites which show "Stock", "Non-Motorized Boat", or "Boat" as the only category of user in the campsite name. 

    • You must be travelling with stock in order to stay at a campsite with "Stock" as the only travel category.

    • You must be travelling by non-motorized boat in order to stay at a campsite with "Non-Motorized Boat" as the only travel category.

    • You must be travelling by boat (either motorized or non-motorized) in order to stay at a campsite with "Boat" as the only travel category.

    • You must be travelling by foot in order to stay at a campsite with "Backpacker" as the only travel category.

  • Food poles or metal boxes are provided at designated campsites. You must bring 30 feet (9m) of rope to secure your food on the provided poles. All food, trash, and scented items must be hung from the food-pole or inside the bear box. Items must be properly secured anytime they’re not directly attended. Approved hard sided bear resistant containers may be used in lieu of hanging. Soft-sided containers must be hung from the food pole or stored in the bear box.

  • Bring a trowel for human waste disposal. Human waste must be disposed of in a pit toilet or buried in a cat hole dug 6-8 inches (15-20 cm) deep at least 100 feet (30.5 m) from water, trails, and campsites. 

  • Pets are not permitted on trails and in the backcountry. 

  • A park entrance fee is required for entry into the National Park. Pay your entry fee in person or online. The park also honors valid America the Beautiful-the National Parks and Federal Recreational Lands passes (also known as an interagency passes, e.g., Senior, 4th Grade, Military, etc.). 

Early Season

  • Backcountry access is limited during May and June due to deep snow and streams swollen from snow melt. Snow and dangerous stream crossing may persist in some areas well into July. Contact the Central Backcountry Office for trip planning assistance. 

Boating

  • Review the park's Boating page for detailed regulations, fees, and safety information.

  • The boating season starts the Saturday of Memorial Day Weekend and extends through October 31.

  • All watercraft, including float tubes and paddle boards, must purchase a Yellowstone boat permit and be inspected for Aquatic Invasive Species (AIS) before launching.

  • AIS inspections and boat permits are available 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM daily at Bridge Bay, Grant Village, and Lewis Lake. Plan accordingly.

  • A 30-day dry time is required for all sailboats and certain complex motorized boats (inboard, inboard/outboard, or inboard jet drives).

  • The following are banned in Yellowstone: watercraft equipped with sealed internal ballast tanks, watercraft with evidence of dead or live mussels, watercraft previously fouled with mussels, regardless of dry time.

Stock Use

  • Contact the Central Backcountry Office for help planning trips with stock.

  • Campsites allowing stock have limits on the annual amount of stock use. Although a campsite may appear to be available, it may have reached its Stock Use Limit and not be available for camping with stock. Reservations are reviewed by staff and subject to change.

  • The earliest a stock trip can start is on July 1st of a given year. Several stock sites have a later opening date due to grazing not being ready.

  • Stock users must possess proof of a negative Coggins test performed within the last 12 months for all equine stock entering Yellowstone.

  • Review Yellowstone’s Stock Regulations for more information.
description.no_show_policy:
No Show Policy: All permits must be issued in person during permit issuing stations hours of operation (8:00 AM-4:30 PM). Permits must be issued and picked up by 10:00 AM on the first day of your permit. 

Your entire reservation will be cancelled as a no show and campsites made available for other groups unless you pick up your permit by 10:00 AM on the first day of the reservation or notify the backcountry office that you will be arriving after 10:00 AM on the first day of the reservation. 

If you are unable to pick up the permit by 10:00 AM, you may contact the Central Backcountry Office at 307-344-2160 to have your permit held until 4:30 PM.
description.quota_details:
Overnight backcountry camping is restricted to designated campsites and areas. The number of parties that may stay overnight in the backcountry is limited by the number of campsites and capacity of individual campsites.

Most campsites are available to be reserved in advance through the early access lottery and a general on sale period. A portion of the campsites are available first-come, first-serve by showing up in person at a backcountry office up to 2 days prior to the start date of a trip.

Each campsite has limits on group size, length of stay, and method of travel permitted. Campsites are available for up to 3 consecutive nights, however some campsites are limited to 1 or 2 nights. Maximum group size ranges from 4 to 12 people. Groups that exceed the campsite size limit will need to obtain an additional reservation and be prepared to cook and sleep as separate groups.
description.season_information:
A permit is required year-round for all overnight stays in the backcountry. A backcountry permit allows the permit holder and their group to camp in a designated campsite. 

You may stay up to 3 consecutive nights at any one campsite unless otherwise noted in the campsite description. Each campsite has a limit to the number of people, stock, and boats permitted. 

Peak Season (May 15-October 31): permits are available through the early access lottery (see important dates, below), regular sales (open April 26-October 31), or in-person at a backcountry office. Pick up permits obtained through the early access lottery or general on-sale in person at a backcountry permit office within 2-days of the trip start date.

Non-Peak Season (November 1-May 14): permits for non-peak season are available beginning October 6. After making a reservation during the non-peak season, email the Central Backcountry Office at yell_backcountry_office@nps.gov within 5-days of the start date to obtain your permit.

4675323304.description:
Gallatin NW Winter camping zone. 

Winter campsites must be in a designated backcountry site or at least ¼ mile from and out of sight of roadways, developed areas, patrol cabins, thermal areas, and other backcountry campers. Undesignated camping permitted December 15-March 31.  

Camping is prohibited within 100 feet of a water source or trail.

Wood fires are not allowed during the winter season.

Camping is prohibited on bare ground and vegetation emerging from snow cover.

Refer to winter camping information

4675323326.name: Wapiti-Broad Creek

4675323327.description:
Pelican Valley winter camping zone

The Park's roads are closed, limited access: in order to get into this area a commercial snow coach ride must be arranged, or a non commercially guided snowmobile permit must be aquired (very limited quantities available).

Winter campsites must be in a designated backcountry site or at least 1/4 mile from and out of sight of roadways, developed areas, patrol cabins, thermal areas, and other backcountry campers. Undesignated camping permitted December 15 - March 14.  

Camping is prohibited within 100 feet of a water source or trail.

Wood fires are not allowed during the winter season.

Camping is prohibited on bare ground and vegetation emerging from snow cover.

Refer to winter camping information .
